chapter: Bands and bandleading in New Orleans
title: Quitting Tony Giardina's band over his sleeping brother
summary: Bergen tells how he lost the St. Bernard Country Club job with Tony Giardina after his teenage brother fell asleep on the bandstand, and describes Giardina's band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, we left out Tony Giardina, who was back before the band.

Oh boy, Tony Giardina. You're going back to 19 when your brother... You know when I quit that band? My old brother, I was trying to teach him trumpet when he was only about 14. He went to sleep on the bandstand. So Tony Giardina says, you're going to get that kid off the bandstand. I said, the kid don't, of course I was drinking them days. I said, the kid don't sleep there, I don't play. That was the end of my job. And my brother-in-law says, you were tough in them days. He's tough now. He's a big rascal. But he said, you were tough in them days. I don't know, I was a kid how you quit that job. But Tony had a pretty good band. He had Sajir Rod, he had Spike Legnan on bass, Charlie, what's Charlie's name? A drum player. I can't think of it. It wasn't Charlie Faber. Tony Giardina's wife played the piano. He had a pretty good library and he could really blow that clarinet on Panama. I remember the night I quit he said he was going to hit me in the head with the saxophone. I said, well don't hit me in the head with the clarinet because you sound pretty good on that. But he tolerated me. He was a nice guy and I was friends with him as long as he lived. But that was just a bad night for me, I guess.
Well, I liked his playing, huh?
He played good. He went up to Chicago with all those guys in the old days. I can't care if he had a drum player's name. Charlie what? He joined the Coast Guard Auxiliary during the war.
That was before I was here. Yeah.

So anyway I played, that was the old St. Bernard Country Club, three times a week I think it was, or twice a week. And I liked it. It was a pretty good job. I liked it. And I liked playing with Tony's band. Until he said my brother-in-law couldn't sleep. My mother-in-law is dead. But it was a good take. And I was always there.
